figures: 1. Figure 1: Overview of the three-phase overlap-resampled L-BFGS training pipeline. Phase 1 uses Adam with full collocation resampling for initial exploration. Phase 2 fixes collocation points to stabilize gradients before L-BFGS. Phase 3 enables continued resampling while maintaining valid curvature estimates through overlap-set gradient computation.

2. Figure 2: L-BFGS behavior under different collocation strategies on the ice-shelf inverse problem. (a) Number of L-BFGS outer iterations before termination. Fixed L-BFGS terminates early (~1234 steps) due to gradient tolerance, while overlap-resampled variants run 4.3× more iterations. (b) Cautious update skips: smaller overlap fractions lead to more curvature pair rejections, but the method remains stable even at o = 0.25.
results_section: 1. Overlap-LBFGS (o = 0.5) achieves the best performance across all metrics, representing a 7% improvement over Adam + Resampling
2. Overlap-LBFGS (o = 0.5) represents a 30% improvement over the standard Adam → Fixed L-BFGS approach
3. Overlap-LBFGS (o = 0.9) achieves 2.1× worse than fixed L-BFGS but 8.5× better than Adam-only
4. Overlap-LBFGS runs 13× more L-BFGS iterations (8240 vs 620) without premature termination
5. accuracy remains comparable: Berr = 8.28 × 10−4 at o = 0.25 versus 8.06 × 10−4 at o = 0.5, a difference within 3% and well within standard deviation

6. Fixed L-BFGS terminates early at approximately 1234 steps due to reaching gradient tolerance, while overlap-resampled variants (o = 0.25 and o = 0.5) run 4.3× more iterations (5307 and 4517 steps respectively) until budget exhaustion
7. Running Overlap-LBFGS from scratch (without Adam warmstart) on the Poisson problem yields relL2 = 1.36 × 10−2, which is 19× worse than with warmstart (7.03 × 10−4)
